title: AI consulting services: what to buy, what it costs, where it pays
description: What AI consulting should deliver, what it costs against hiring a team or buying software, and the finance work where AI pays first. With our own data.
summary: AI consulting should turn one business problem into a working system that you can prove works. Most pilots never show up in the P&L. The ones that do start with a number to move, a benchmark on the company's own files, and a plan for keeping the system right after launch.
verdict: Hire AI consulting for one problem with a number attached, not for a strategy deck. A good engagement benchmarks the options on your own files first, builds the winner into your workflow, and keeps checking it as models change. Model choice alone can decide whether a project pays: in our document benchmark, tools that found nearly the same facts differed 48 times in cost.

example.input: A mid-sized lender wants AI to read small-business loan files so underwriters stop retyping bank statements.
example.output: A benchmark of the leading models on 50 of the lender's own files with the cost per file for each, the winner built into the loan system with a review queue, and a monthly re-check as new models ship.

recipes.name: 1. Benchmark first
recipes.when: Before anyone writes production code. Settles which approach wins on your files and what it costs.
flow: Pick one job with a number to move
Answers your team checked, locked first
recipes.cost: A short fixed-scope project. You keep the files, the answer key and the code, so you can re-run it.

recipes.name: 2. Build the winner into the work
recipes.when: Once the benchmark shows a clear winner that pays back.
flow: Go live on a share of volume
recipes.cost: Depends on the systems it touches. Gartner warns that production can cost far more than the pilot, so scope it from the benchmark, not the demo.

recipes.name: 3. Keep it right
recipes.when: Always. Models, prices and your documents change.
recipes.cost: Small, because the benchmark already exists. This is where most of the long-run savings come from.

testTitle: How to benchmark a consultant's claims before you sign
howToTest: Ask for a benchmark on 20 to 50 of your own files before you sign for a full build.
Agree the right answers with your own team first, and lock them, so the result is graded against your standard.
Ask for cost per correct answer, not price per token. The cheapest-looking model is not always the cheapest to run.
Ask what happens when a better model ships next month. If the answer is a new project, the system will go stale.
Ask for a client where the system has run in production for at least six months.

buyVsBuild.buy: Hire a consultant when you need one system working this quarter, have no AI engineers, and want someone accountable for the result. Pay for a fixed scope with a benchmark you can check.
buyVsBuild.build: Hire in-house when AI is core to what you sell and you will run many systems. Expect months to hire and the salaries above.

watchOuts: Firms that resell one software vendor's product and call it a recommendation.
Demos on clean sample data that never meet your real files.
No answer key: without agreed right answers, nobody can show the system works.
Budgets that stop at the pilot. Gartner expects at least half of generative AI projects to overrun through 2028, and running the model is most of the lifetime cost.

rules.name: EU AI Act, Annex III
rules.what: Credit scoring of people and life and health insurance pricing are high-risk uses. Any consultant building them for EU operations should plan logging, oversight and documentation from day one.

rules.name: Regulation B, 12 CFR 1002.9
rules.what: US lenders must give the specific main reasons for a decline within 30 days, whatever model made it.

rules.name: NYDFS Circular Letter No. 7
rules.what: New York insurers must test AI and outside data for unfair discrimination, keep board oversight, stay responsible for vendor tools and give specific reasons and data sources for adverse decisions.

rules.name: NAIC Model Bulletin on AI
rules.what: Insurers need a written AI program with governance, risk controls and vendor oversight. California, Colorado and New York have their own rules instead.

rules.name: Colorado SB21-169
rules.status: Life; auto and health from 15 Oct 2025
rules.what: Insurers must test outside data and models for unfair discrimination, fix harm found and report to the Division.
